{{Short description|Official UK socio-economic classification}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2025}}
{{Use British English|date=February 2015}}
The '''National Statistics Socio-economic Classification''' (often abbreviated to '''NS-SEC''') is the official socio-economic classification in the United Kingdom. It is an adaptation of the [[Class stratification|Goldthorpe schema]] which was first known as the Nuffield Class Schema developed in the 1970s.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Constant Flux: A Study of Class Mobility in Industrial Societies|last=Erikson|first=Robert|last2=Goldthorpe|first2=John|publisher=Clarendon Press|year=1992|isbn=0198273835|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=A Researcher's Guide to the National Statistics Socio-economic Classification|last=Rose|first=David|last2=Pevalin|first2=David (eds)|publisher=Sage|year=2003|isbn=0761973222|location=London}}</ref> It was developed using the Standard Occupational Classification 1990 (SOC90) and rebased on the Standard Occupational Classification 2000 (SOC2000) before its first major use on the [[2001 United Kingdom census|2001 UK census.]]<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book|title=The ESRC Review of Government Social Classifications|last=Rose|first=David|last2=O'Reilly|first2=Karen|publisher=ONS/ESRC|year=1998|isbn=1857742915|location=London/Swindon}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Constructing Classes: Towards a New Social Classification for the UK|last=Rose|first=David|last2=O'Reilly|first2=Karen (eds)|publisher=ESRC/ONS|year=1997|isbn=0862262542|location=Swindon/London}}</ref> The NS-SEC replaced two previous social classifications: Socio-economic Groups (SEG) and Social Class based on Occupation (SC, formerly known as Registrar General's Social Class, RGSC). The NS-SEC was [https://www.ons.gov.uk/methodology/classificationsandstandards/standardoccupationalclassificationsoc/soc2010/soc2010volume3thenationalstatisticssocioeconomicclassificationnssecrebasedonsoc2010 rebased on the Standard Occupational Classification 2010] prior to the [[2011 United Kingdom census|2011 UK census]] and it will be further rebased on the new Standard Occupational Classification 2020 for use on the 2021 UK census.

The NS-SEC is a nested classification. It has 14 operational categories, with some sub-categories, and is commonly used in eight-class, five-class, and three-class versions.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The National Statistics Socio-economic Classification: Origins, Development and Use|last=Rose|first=David|last2=Pevalin|first2=David|last3=(with O'Reilly|first3=Karen)|publisher=ONS|year=2003|isbn=1403996482|location=London}}</ref> Only the three-category version is intended to represent any form of [[hierarchy]]. The version intended for most users (the analytic version) has eight classes:

# Higher [[Management|managerial]] and [[professional]] occupations
# Lower managerial and professional occupations
# Intermediate occupations (clerical, sales, service)
# Small [[employer]]s and own account workers
# Lower supervisory and [[Technology|technical]] occupations
# Semi-routine occupations
# Routine occupations
# Never worked or long-term unemployed

The three-class version is reduced to following:
#Higher occupations
#Intermediate occupations
#Lower occupations
